facts.claim: KDA's chunk kernels are slow because of an inter-chunk serial dependency
facts.value: REFUTED. Three independent measurements: (1) time scales LINEARLY with B*h (work-scaled 0.98 from B=8) -- a chain's latency does not grow with batch; (2) halving chunk_size to 32 DOUBLES the chain length and is 19% FASTER (T=4096: 12.12 -> 9.81 ms), the reverse of the chain prediction; (3) the genuinely sequential kernels (fwd_kernel_h grid 512, bwd_kernel_dhu grid 256) are 1.51 of 12.77 ms = 11.9% of KDA time. The real cause is OCCUPANCY: the four dominant kernels achieve 6-12% occupancy and run at 15-29% of HBM and 16-42% of SM, while every kernel above 80% occupancy runs at 85-93% of HBM peak. Grid size is ample (8192-131072 blocks on 78 SMs); the kernels burn too many registers/shared memory per block, leaving ~4-8 resident warps with nothing to hide memory latency. Latency-bound, not chain-bound, not bandwidth-bound, not grid-bound. Measured DRAM traffic: 14.79 GB in 12.77 ms = 1.16 TB/s, 29% of the 4 TB/s peak.
facts.uncertainty: one layer in isolation, uncompiled and without fp8; the in-model kernels could differ. The T-sweep criterion (ns/token flat from T=1024) is weak on its own -- proofs 1 and 2 are what discriminate.
facts.boundary: the occupancy lives inside fla's Triton/TileLang kernels. Fixing it means editing or rewriting fla, and rewriting is already refuted (tileRL measured its own TileLang GDN 9.3x slower than fla on H20).
facts.refuted_by: an ncu run showing high occupancy in the dominant KDA kernels

Applied to the in-model fla group (~102 of the 128.1 ms DeltaRecurrence total; short_conv is unaffected) that is ~19.5 ms/step, 2.0% of the 978.5 ms step.
facts.uncertainty: the intra-chunk work is O(chunk^2) so halving it halves that term, which is why more serial steps still wins. NOT tested: chunk_size changes the chunking of the same math, so numerics shift slightly.

facts.value: The training loss path slices head.weight[:Cfg.vocab] into Liger FLCE, which has no per-class mask: the alignment-padding rows (vocab_real:vocab) entered the softmax denominator at their random-init values. Inference (lm_logits) masks at vocab_real; the training path never did. Fixed 2026-08-30 by zero-initializing the padding rows after self.apply(self._init) (commit 06d52cd): padding logits stay 0, and the rows are never targets so CE gradient only pushes them down. The padding's measured contribution is the constant offset log(32784/32773) = 0.00034 (step-0 delta in every run). The 32776 A/B passed not because the defect was absent but because 3 random columns rarely spike; the defect existed there too, and the zero-init fix is what makes both configs clean.
facts.source: runs/ab_vocab.log (32773 vs 32776), runs/ab_vocab_32784.log, runs/ab_vocab_32784_zeroinit.log, runs/ab_vocab_32784_lr003.log (pod); train.py FLCE slice head.weight[:Cfg.vocab]; fix commit 06d52cd

facts.uncertainty: The +-1.7 swings at LR_SCALE=0.1 were first misattributed to the padding rows; the zero-init run swung identically, proving the swings are chaotic-regime compounding of the width difference itself (the baseline arm 32773 trains smoothly on the old sample in the 32776 A/B but chaotically on the rebuilt sample at LR 0.1). The padding rows' own contribution is the 0.0003 constant offset, isolated at step 0. Single run per cell.
facts.boundary: The A/B's three criteria (max |delta| at noise floor, no growth, no systematic sign) are only meaningful in a STABLE training regime; in a chaotic regime they fail for any width change. The 32776 pass was regime-luck as much as column-count luck. This is the criteria's ceiling, not an execution failure -- same family as b0's 8.4pt (formula right, wrong source) and corpus_fp_matches reporting 1/7 yet PASS: a check that passes for reasons unrelated to what it checks. Run the vocab A/B at AB_LR_SCALE=0.03 (the stable regime on the current sample; 0.1 swings +-1.7).

config.command: setsid nohup bash -c 'cd /work/tilerl && export PYTHONPATH=/work/tilerl/src:/work/tilerl/packages/tilerl-kernels/src TILELANG_CACHE_DIR=/work/tilelang_cache TILERL_TARGET=cuda TILERL_QWEN38_SOURCE=/data00/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 && python -m tilerl.cli serve --model qwen38-27b --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100 --devices 0,1 >> /work/tilerl/serve27b.log 2>&1' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
config.devices: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 then --devices 0,1 (one engine replica per visible card)
config.cuda_graph: ON. Engine.__init__ sets _decode_graph_on = decode_graph and draft is None; serve takes no --draft, so the graph stays on. Passing a draft would silently disable it and cost 7.9x at B=1 (11.6 -> 91.6 ms/tick).

facts.uncertainty: only a single-request smoke test; no throughput or concurrency measurement. Sized for the 400-document validation, not for the full 216-shard corpus.
facts.boundary: the service is this session's; scoring prompts, acceptance criteria and their facts belong to the scoring session
